stories.title: "ADHD-friendly design" checklists are general UX tips, and the evidence for Bionic Reading does not hold up
stories.blurb: Kristian Mikhel argues that reducing clutter and memory load is ordinary UX with a new label. He points instead to a 2025 web framework co-designed with neurodivergent users and prototyped by two designers with ADHD, and to a framework that also governs how the team works: rewards for daily use are fine, using anxiety or fear of missing out to drive them is not.

stories.title: Day Job gives Lance Oppenheim's To Be Formed one main wordmark and twenty spares to swap in
stories.blurb: The LA studio built the identity for the production company from references like off-kilter book covers and early-2000s DVD menus, with thick forms next to thin calligraphic letters at different x-heights. The primary mark merges about twenty secondary wordmarks the client can rotate, so the name, which started as a placeholder, stays visibly unfinished.

stories.title: Studio Herrström builds Sony's Milkshake label on car window stickers and road signs
stories.blurb: The name came up on a drive, so the Vienna studio made the car the recurring motif: Context Type’s Gates in sticker-style lockups, road-sign icons, and the old identity’s bright palette shifted toward milkshake flavours. Ordinary structure carries the system as the label scales, the lightning logomark carries the energy.

stories.title: VisitOSLO's Halfdan returns, and the sequel changes genre because the surprise is spent
stories.blurb: The 2024 film with the gloomy local who talks people out of visiting drew more than 25 million organic views. NewsLab's agency lead says the first one worked because it was unexpected, so they did not remake it for winter and turned it into a Christmas horror musical instead, which logged over five million views in launch week.

stories.title: An AI agent's confession is generated the same way as its mistake, so it is not a record
stories.blurb: Dora Czerna starts with Replit’s agent deleting Jason Lemkin’s live database, apologising fluently, then wrongly claiming rollback was impossible. Her point for anyone reviewing agent work: an agent’s account of what it did is a summary generated after the fact, and visible reasoning is produced alongside the answer, so it deserves the distrust designers long since apply to people describing their own behaviour.

sources.name: UX Collective
sources.headline: Can you take AI at its word?
sources.author: Dora Czerna

stories.title: Ars Technica's creative director on Apple Music's making-of: the process footage is the proof
stories.blurb: TBWA/Media Arts Lab and Fred again.. shot the new branding through a tank of mineral oil driven by a transducer, so sound became ripples on printed panels. The author is no fan of Liquid Glass, but argues that when any image might be prompted, showing the hands at work is what makes viewers value the result.
